title: Managing school transport — a practical guide for day and mixed schools
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on managing school transport safely and efficiently — routes, driver management, and parent communication.
body:
For day schools and mixed day-boarding schools, school transport is both a significant operational responsibility and a genuine safety matter. A poorly managed transport system creates daily friction with parents, safety risk for students, and unnecessary cost. A well-managed one runs quietly in the background — which is exactly the goal.

Route planning grounded in real data

Transport routes designed once and never revisited often become inefficient as student residence patterns shift over time. Reviewing routes at the start of each year against actual current student addresses — rather than assuming the existing routes remain optimal — identifies opportunities to reduce costs and travel time for students.

Driver and vehicle standards

  • All drivers hold valid, appropriate licences and have been vetted, including background checks given they are responsible for children's safety
  • Vehicles meet NTSA safety standards and undergo regular maintenance checks, not only when a problem becomes apparent
  • A designated staff member (often a matron or transport coordinator) accompanies routes where student numbers or ages warrant additional supervision
  • Clear protocols for student pickup and drop-off, including what happens if a parent or guardian is not present at drop-off

Non-negotiable safety standard: Every vehicle used for school transport should have a clear, tested emergency protocol — communicated to drivers and staff — for breakdowns, accidents, or medical emergencies during transit. This should never be improvised for the first time during an actual incident.

Communication with parents about transport

Parents relying on school transport want reliable, predictable information — pickup times, route changes, and prompt notification of any delays. A WhatsApp broadcast system for transport updates, rather than relying on students to relay information or parents calling the school office, significantly reduces daily transport-related enquiries and builds parent confidence in the system.

Managing transport costs transparently

Transport fees should be calculated based on actual route costs — fuel, driver salary, maintenance, insurance — not arbitrary figures. Being able to explain to parents how transport fees are calculated, particularly if an increase is needed, maintains trust in a cost that parents often scrutinise closely.

Handling incidents and complaints promptly

Transport-related complaints — a late pickup, a safety concern about a driver, overcrowding on a route — should have a clear, prompt response process. Parents who feel transport complaints are ignored quickly lose confidence in the whole system, even if the underlying issue is relatively minor.

Reviewing transport as part of overall school safety

Transport safety deserves the same deliberate attention as other school safety domains covered in emergency preparedness planning — reviewed periodically, not assumed to be adequate simply because no incident has occurred yet.
